cases.title: History notebook · A food counter on the street

blocks.label: Title
blocks.text: A food counter on the street

blocks.label: Encounter
blocks.text: The game represents a counter and inset jar forms. This is a schematic model of the food-counter setting.

blocks.label: Claim
blocks.text: The thermopolium, or food-and-drink counter, of Vetutius Placidus had large storage jars built into its serving counter.

blocks.label: Evidence
blocks.text: The Park describes the surviving counter and its embedded vessels.

blocks.label: Limits
blocks.text: A counter does not establish its exact daily menu or the identity of everyone who worked there.

blocks.label: Game Changed
blocks.text: Sabina, her stock, prices and the flour dispute are fictional. The model is not a surveyed reconstruction.

blocks.label: Question
blocks.text: Which visible feature suggests that customers were served here?

blocks.label: Rights
blocks.text: Original prose and schematic game geometry. No external image reproduced.

blocks.label: Source
blocks.text: Archaeological Park of Pompeii: Along the streets of Pompeii · https://pompeiisites.org/en/pompeii-map/analysis/along-the-streets-of-pompeii/

cases.title: History notebook · A home turned into a workplace

blocks.label: Title
blocks.text: A home turned into a workplace

blocks.label: Encounter
blocks.text: The game represents washing basins inside a simplified workshop.

blocks.label: Claim
blocks.text: The Fullonica of Stephanus was a cloth-cleaning workshop adapted from a house. Fullonica means a fullery, where cloth was processed.

blocks.label: Evidence
blocks.text: Washing facilities and changes to the domestic building support its workshop interpretation.

blocks.label: Limits
blocks.text: The conventional building name does not establish every occupant or worker. Precise ownership can be an interpretation.

blocks.label: Game Changed
blocks.text: Chreste, her schedule and the paid shifts offered to Aelia are invented. Chreste is enslaved; Aelia taking a paid shift is a different situation.

blocks.label: Question
blocks.text: What would distinguish a workshop from a room used only for domestic life?

blocks.label: Rights
blocks.text: Original prose and schematic game geometry. No external image reproduced.

blocks.label: Source
blocks.text: Archaeological Park of Pompeii: Along the streets of Pompeii · https://pompeiisites.org/en/pompeii-map/analysis/along-the-streets-of-pompeii/

cases.title: History notebook · A person who had been freed

blocks.label: Title
blocks.text: A person who had been freed

blocks.label: Encounter
blocks.text: Aelia is a fictional freedwoman: she was enslaved and was later freed.

blocks.label: Claim
blocks.text: Naevoleia Tyche’s commemorative monument and inscription identify her as a freedwoman.

blocks.label: Evidence
blocks.text: The Park discusses the inscription on the monument near the Herculaneum Gate. That monument is outside this game district.

blocks.label: Limits
blocks.text: One prominent monument cannot show how every freedwoman lived. Women had varied social statuses and opportunities. The Park’s imagined first-person narration is modern interpretation.

blocks.label: Game Changed
blocks.text: Aelia is not Naevoleia Tyche. Her money, work, access and choices are fictional simplifications, not general Roman legal rights.

blocks.label: Question
blocks.text: Can one prosperous individual stand for everyone who had been freed?

blocks.label: Rights
blocks.text: Original prose and schematic game geometry. No external image reproduced.

blocks.text: Archaeological Park of Pompeii: Nevoleia Tyche · https://pompeiisites.org/en/exhibitions-and-events/nevoleia-tyche-en/

cases.title: History notebook · Political messages on walls

blocks.label: Title
blocks.text: Political messages on walls

blocks.label: Encounter
blocks.text: This learning card describes surviving painted notices. It does not identify a game wall as an excavated inscription.

blocks.label: Claim
blocks.text: Pompeian electoral notices named candidates, the offices sought and supporters.

blocks.label: Evidence
blocks.text: The Naples museum presents painted inscription fragments and explains their recurring forms.

blocks.label: Limits
blocks.text: An endorsement does not establish an election result or equal political rights for every resident.

blocks.label: Game Changed
blocks.text: There is no voting mechanic here. Aelia reading this card implies no eligibility for office. Any decorative wall marks in the model are reconstruction, not quoted ancient text.

blocks.label: Question
blocks.text: What can an endorsement tell you, and what can it leave unknown?

cases.title: History notebook · Evidence, reconstruction and invented choices

blocks.label: Title
blocks.text: Evidence, reconstruction and invented choices

blocks.label: Encounter
blocks.text: Compare the represented counter or workshop with the delivery dispute you are playing.

blocks.label: Claim
blocks.text: Buildings, objects and inscriptions can support limited historical claims. They do not preserve Sabina’s conversation with Aelia.

blocks.label: Evidence
blocks.text: The linked Park descriptions discuss surviving structures; the museum shows inscribed objects.

blocks.label: Limits
blocks.text: Evidence leaves gaps. A plausible reconstruction remains an interpretation.

blocks.label: Game Changed
blocks.text: Every named game character, exact price, reward, deadline, relationship score and cart agreement is invented for play. The miniature street network is simplified.
